reviewedFields.audience.programmeDescription: Chinese Studies at Leiden combines Mandarin and Classical Chinese with the study of China’s history, culture, politics, economy and society. Students develop language and research skills, normally spend a period studying Mandarin in China or Taiwan, and complete an independent paper linked to a third-year seminar. Elective choices allow a disciplinary emphasis; these are not separate formal specialisations.
reviewedFields.audience.comparisonExplanation: A complete UCR comparison is not yet available because the official third-year language-choice requirements conflict. The supported curriculum is shown below. This uncertainty does not establish that UCR offers no suitable study possibilities.

audience.curriculum.routeLabel: Chinese Studies; political economy and society choices
audience.curriculum.limitation: The listed requirements total 175 EC and include 30 EC of elective space. A further language choice is required, but the official rules disagree about whether it is 5 EC overall or 5 EC in each semester. The paper and its linked seminar are counted together as 10 EC. This is an incomplete curriculum, not a certified 180-EC degree plan.

audience.componentNotes.y2-mandarin-2c-abroad: One 15-EC language-training period in China or Taiwan. Participation requires the completed first year and the applicable cohort and departure conditions. A programme in Leiden is available only under specified circumstances.
audience.componentNotes.y3-ba-paper: The linked seminar and independent paper together carry 10 EC. A completed first year, permission and supervision arrangements are required.
audience.componentNotes.y3-elective-space: 30 EC of elective space, subject to Leiden’s requirements. The Chinese Economy and Society minor cannot be used because of overlap with compulsory study.
